identity.title: OSHA Form 300A Summary of Work-Related Injuries and Illnesses, Calendar Year 2025, Portland Facility
identity.issuer: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC (certified by Daniel Okafor, Plant Manager), on the federal OSHA form
identity.site: Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210

scan.summary: This is the company's own 2025 annual injury and illness summary for the Portland facility (page 1). It shows 3 recordable injuries: 1 with 6 days away from work and 2 other recordable cases. There were no deaths, no job-transfer cases and no illnesses, among an average of 65 employees working 128,400 hours. It is a record, not a program. It proves that the 2025 summary was completed and certified on February 1, 2026. It does not prove that it was posted, that the underlying 300 Log and 801 forms are complete, or that it was submitted electronically to OSHA.
scan.freshness_note: This is the latest annual summary that can exist today. The 2026 summary is not due until February 1, 2027. The required posting period for this summary (February 1 to April 30, 2026) has ended. You must keep it, with the 2025 OSHA 300 Log and DCBS 801 forms, for 5 years after the end of 2025, which is through December 31, 2030.

gaps.title: No proof of electronic submission to OSHA
gaps.description: Oregon rule OAR 437-001-0700(24)(b) says establishments with 20 to 249 employees in industries listed in its Table 7 must submit their 300A data each year through federal OSHA's Injury Tracking Application (ITA) by March 2. This site had 65 employees. I have not confirmed that NAICS 4246 is on Table 7, but wholesale industries largely are. Nothing in your holdings shows the 2025 data was submitted.
gaps.fix: Check whether NAICS 4246 is on Table 7 of OAR 437-001-0700. If it is, log into the ITA and confirm the 2025 300A was submitted by March 2, 2026. If it was not, submit it now. Keep the ITA confirmation with this summary.

gaps.title: Industry code may not match what the company actually does
gaps.description: The form lists the site as a chemical merchant wholesaler (NAICS 424690) that repackages chemicals. The company profile says chemical manufacturing, and the site holds an air permit with scrubbers and carbon controls. If the site actually manufactures or blends products, the correct code could be in NAICS 325. That would change which electronic-submission tables apply to you.
gaps.fix: Confirm the correct NAICS code for the Portland site's main activity. Use the same code on the 300A, in the ITA, and in your other filings.

scan.confidence_notes: The single page was fully readable, and everything in the identity section and facts comes from it. The case totals add up: 1 + 0 + 2 = 3 cases, which matches the 3 injuries listed. The hours are reasonable for 65 employees. A Plant Manager signing is likely acceptable as the highest-ranking official at the site, but I did not check who counts as a company executive under the rule. I am not sure whether NAICS 4246 is on Oregon's Table 7, so the electronic-submission gap is marked as inferred. The form prints 'Rev. 01/2004'. I believe the federal form has a different revision label, but I did not check, and Oregon accepts equivalent forms, so I did not list it as a gap. I cannot tell from this page whether the summary was actually posted from February to April 2026.
